title: U.S. House · Indiana's 5th District
area: Central Indiana, including the northern Indianapolis suburbs (Hamilton, Madison, and surrounding counties)

context.text: Incumbent Victoria Spartz won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary over Scott King, 59.9% to 40.1%. J.D. Ford, an Indiana state senator, won a seven-candidate Democratic primary with 42.5% of the vote.

candidates.name: Victoria Spartz
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary over Scott King, 59.9% to 40.1%

summary.text: Victoria Spartz is the Republican incumbent for Indiana's 5th District. Born in Ukraine, she immigrated to the United States in 2000, worked as an accountant and finance executive and started several businesses, served in the Indiana Senate from 2017 to 2020, and was elected to Congress in 2020.

background.text: Born in Nosivka, Ukraine, in 1978; immigrated to the United States in 2000 after meeting her husband, Jason, and became a U.S. citizen, according to her official biography.

Earned a bachelor's degree in international economics and an MBA from the National University of Economics in Ukraine, and a Master of Professional Accountancy (listed by Ballotpedia as an M.P.A.) from Indiana University's Kelley School of Business in 2006; also completed a Harvard Business School executive education program on health care.

Worked as a certified public accountant and auditor, including at Big 4 public accounting firms for Fortune 500 companies, and taught as an adjunct faculty member at Indiana University's Kelley School of Business.
Served as chief financial officer at the Indiana Attorney General's Office and started several businesses in financial consulting, farming and real estate, according to her official biography.
Served in the Indiana Senate (District 20) from 2017 to 2020.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2020 and took office in 2021, succeeding Rep. Susan Brooks; re-elected in 2022 and 2024.

Serves on the Joint Economic Committee in the 119th Congress and, according to her official biography, leads working groups on healthcare and budget reforms; previously served on the House Judiciary Committee.
Lives in Noblesville with her husband, Jason, and their two daughters, according to her official biography.

priorities.text: Campaign website says the national debt should be tackled through spending cuts and welfare reform rather than by raising taxes, and calls for balancing the budget.
priorities.quote: The debt can be tackled, not by raising taxes on US citizens, but by taking a critical look at the unnecessary spending of the federal government.

priorities.text: Campaign website says the legal immigration process should be reformed, including a more robust work visa program, to better curb illegal immigration.
priorities.quote: If we want to curb illegal immigration, we need to address our legal immigration process to better serve our national interest and have a more robust work visa program.

priorities.text: Campaign website lists preserving Second Amendment freedoms and protecting the sanctity of human life among her constitutional priorities.
priorities.quote: We must preserve our 2nd Amendment freedoms against the tyranny of the government, and protect the sanctity of all human life.

record.text: Assigned to the Joint Economic Committee for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Served on the House Judiciary Committee during the 118th Congress (2023-2024), including its Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust subcommittee.

candidates.name: J.D. Ford
candidates.ballotNote: Won a seven-candidate May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 42.5% of the vote
candidates.currentRole: Indiana State Senator, District 29 (2018-2026; not seeking re-election to the state Senate)

summary.text: J.D. Ford is the Democratic nominee for Indiana's 5th District. A former fraternity executive and nonprofit professional, he has represented Indiana Senate District 29 since 2018 as the first openly LGBTQ+ member of the General Assembly and is not seeking re-election to the state Senate. His campaign emphasizes affordability, healthcare and care costs.

background.text: According to his Candidate Connection survey, learned the value of hard work from his father, a union truck driver, and his mother, an assisted living administrator, and was influenced by grandparents who served as local officials.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science and criminal justice from the University of Akron (2005) and a master's degree in education from Purdue University (2010).
Worked as senior director of recruitment and expansion for Theta Chi Fraternity, Inc.; Ballotpedia lists his profession as nonprofit professional.
Elected to Indiana Senate District 29 on November 6, 2018, defeating Republican incumbent Mike Delph; took office November 7, 2018, and was re-elected in 2022.
Describes himself as the first, and so far only, openly LGBTQ+ member of the Indiana General Assembly.

Serves on the Indiana Senate's Commerce and Technology, Education and Career Development, Health and Provider Services, Elections, Family & Children Services, Homeland Security and Transportation, Utilities, and Veterans Affairs and the Military committees in the 2025-2026 session; earlier he served as ranking minority member of several committees and vice chair of the Ethics Committee.

priorities.text: Names affordability as a top message, saying he would work to block what he describes as anti-competitive hospital, insurance, and grocery mergers.
priorities.quote: We have a monopoly problem, and I'm going to tackle it by restoring competition to the market. I'll work to block anti-competitive hospital and insurance mergers, block grocery mega-mergers that kill local choice, and ensure our utility bills don't skyrocket just to subsidize energy-hungry data centers for massive corporations.

priorities.text: Names care costs (childcare and senior care) as a priority, calling for an expanded child and dependent care tax credit and national minimum staffing standards for nursing homes.
Says he would maintain an open-door policy with regular town halls, as he did in the Statehouse.

positions.summary: Says he wants to take on the president’s tariff policies, citing farmers unable to sell their harvests.
positions.quote: We gotta take on the president's chaotic and erratic tariff policies that have left our farmers with silos of harvests that they can't sell.

positions.summary: Says enforcement is needed against “hardened criminals” but that the administration’s efforts have gone too far, and calls for ICE accountability, warrant-based enforcement and a path to citizenship.
positions.quote: I think we can all agree we need the enforcement to get the hardened criminals out of our country, but I think with this administration's efforts, they've gone a little too far.

record.text: Elected to the Indiana Senate in 2018, flipping the previously Republican-held District 29.

Serves on the Indiana Senate's Commerce and Technology, Education and Career Development, Health and Provider Services, Elections, Family & Children Services, Homeland Security and Transportation, Utilities, and Veterans Affairs and the Military committees during the 2025-2026 session.

researchNotes: Victoria Spartz has not completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; her spartz.house.gov Issues pages (Congress, Economy, Education, Health, Veterans) contain only press-release headlines with no current first-person statements. Positions and priorities are drawn from her campaign website's Issues page instead; her committee record is documented separately. Ballotpedia's sponsored-legislation table for J.D. Ford did not render in the fetched page, so specific bill numbers are not included; his committee assignments and campaign statements are used instead. Ford's and Spartz's early-life details come mainly from Ballotpedia and Spartz's official biography.
